interactions.title: Candrosa guides the initiation and Shakun’s vision
lines: DM: Um, and because... So Candrosa also spends some time sort of telling you about, about the, the sort of history of the initiation ceremony, and he says it'll be a little bit strange because you've already experienced some of it.

DM: Um, having gone through this ritual before without the heart. Um, but what is different is that now the presence of the heart will be there to guide you, and things that didn't make sense may make more sense, he hopes. Um, and the initiation itself is also the story of-
DM: ... Shakun's, not exactly her history, but her power and her sort of spirit and connection to Dunmar.

DM: And so after a week of training and meditation and prayer, um, the, the last evening before the Feast of Bhishma, so the night before, so next... We'll start the session the morning after the initiation. Um, he takes you down again to the... through the temple to the same room that you were in previously, down through the common area of the temple, um, down underground into this cavern where there's a pool of glowing water.

DM: Except that now the room is brightly lit, and you can see that there, instead of a dark room before, um, there is a, there is, um, a warm glow that comes from the rock all around this, the chamber that, um, all around the, the walls-

DM: ... that surround this pool of water in the middle of this chamber. They're just glowing sort of burnished red like the sunset. Basically walked into a, a, a living sunset almost, or sunrise. So everything is warm and, and bright.
DM: Um, and he says, "This is the power of Shakun's heart. With her here, the mesa is alive, bright and powerful and not dark."

DM: And as before, he, um, you change into the robes of the initiates, and he paints a, um, a crescent on your forehead with this red ochre pigment made from the mesa itself, which now also is glowing. And you feel this glow sort of suffuse into you in this, um... It's almost as if you feel somebody, uh, something kind of wrapping its arm around your spirit, around your aura, and leading you to, um, to this, this water, this pool of water.

DM: And just as before, the, the priest, the acolyte who's helping with the ceremony... You know, this is-- You're the only two ones, um, participating in this because, you know, normally there would be... There's a cycle. There's initiation every year or something like that. That already happened, um, and, and you're sort of being initiated off cycle. But because of the circumstances, Candrosa has been in favor of this. So it's just the two of you.

DM: Um, but as before, the, um, the flames of the pool, the p- surface of the pool bursts into this blue light, um, and the a- the acolyte leads you to the pool, gives you a drink of something, and submerges you underneath the flames.

DM: And as before, for a moment, everything is darkness until your vision adjusts and you're looking down now, um, at, um... You're, you're flying over the land of Dunmar from west to east. So starting in this tumbled scrubland of rock and grass and low hills near the border of Chardon, along the outskirts of the mountains that are Drikod's home, and then turning south along the river, um, passing across the plains and into the desert. Then a, turning west again to the Yuvanti Mountains, flying up, approaching the mountains and soaring over the steep high peaks of the mountains and looking at the, um, the savannas and to the, to the south, the lush jungles beyond the mountains.

DM: And as you fly across this land, you can, your, you can feel yourself being, being buoyed up by some presence, and it's, and you're circling around the mesa basically, which is at the center of this land. And as you circle around, the land becomes almost a blur almost. Um, the plains, the, the tall grasses of the, of the north, the deserts. Um, and you dr- as you drift higher and higher, um, you hear a voice, maybe Candrosa's, you're not entirely sure, um, that says, "Look to the past."

DM: And the land changes. And now before you, you see this vast forest covering the entire land. A m- massive forest, like huge trees, um, stretching as far as the eye can see. Um, the sound, occasional sound of singing in a strange language, dancing across the top of the trees. And the voice says again, "This is what was here before."
Unknown: Where's the mesa in the forest?

DM: Uh, the, the mesa is, um... It's not, it's not quite directly in the center of the forest. Um, it's, it's a bit north of the center of the forest. The forest stretches south all the way down to the coast.
Kenzo: I, I guess what I'm asking is, like, where the mesa is now, you know, which obviously is, like-
Kenzo: ... significant. Like, when the forest was there, is there, like, a huge tree there?
DM: Oh, yeah. You can still s-

DM: So it, so it's not a mesa, y- but you can still see it. There is a, um... So, so you can still see a, uh... It's actually, um... What's the, like, inverse of a mesa? [laughs] It's like a, like a... It goes down, right?
DM: It's like a, a big open sinkhole or something like that.
DM: I don't know what the word for that is.
Kenzo: Like a valley, but like a...
DM: But, like, sharp sided, but not like a canyon, because it's in the forest. There's trees growing up around it.

DM: There's, there's actually one enormous tree that, like, is stretching, making this arch across, um, uh, from the side of the, of the, um, of the, of this, like, canyon wall around the pits to the, to the center. There's just these trees that... These, like, a massive, massive trees that grow. These, you know, 500-foot-long branches that form these arches that connect from the stone into the living tree. It's clearly a, a significant place, but it looks different. But you can recognize it. It's still this-
DM: ... still an obvious feature on the landscape.

DM: Um, and as you're watching this, the, the, um, the, the voice, the narration, um, says, "And then evil came." And there's a flash of light, and then the fi- the forest just starts burning. And it starts burning in all directions. It just starts to turn to ash. The fire spreads. Everything's red with flame, and you see nothing but the ash and the dead trees scattered across the land, and the smell of death and blood. And the image slowly fades, uh, to, to almost translucent, so you're sort of looking at a shadowy, um, the same landscape, but a shadowy realm. And things were dark.
Kenzo: When it said, uh, "When evil came," like, what did it look like? Like, what destroyed the forest? Like, was it like a-
DM: A- all you see is fire.
DM: Um, there's no, there's no visual image of anything other than fire marching across the land. You don't really know if that is, like, just metaphorical or if that was an actual fire.

DM: Um, and then there is, um, wave, sort of a w- several waves that come of, of, of... It's almost like the land itself is, like, p- pulsing, like, um, expanding and shrinking, expanding and shrinking.

DM: Um, many settled, and you can see cities begin to spring up on the land below. But the evil was still there. And as these cities start to spring up, at the center of each one, there is a, um... It's, it's almost like there's, like, a little bit of the reflection of the fire in these cities.
DM: Like somehow the fire wasn't totally put out, and the cities kind of encapsulate the fire.

DM: Until death and destruction claimed the land again. And from each of these cities, this red ooze bubbling spreads across the land. And again, everything that was living there turns dark and blackened. It's almost like acid is spilling out across this landscape that you're looking at. Um-
Kenzo: What, what is... Is, is Shakun, like, relevant? Like, does Shakun exist in all this, or this is all before Shakun?
DM: This is all before. This is before Shakun.
Drikod: What, what are the m- what's happening closer to the mountains? Are the, the cities that are farther north having the same thing?
DM: Yeah. I mean, it spreads from the south to the north.
DM: Um, [clears throat] and then, so it's, as it spreads, it's like acid pouring across the land. Everything is being blackened. Everything is, um, being corroded and worn away.
DM: And then everything again sort of turns translucent. And then the voice says again, "Until the land was, land was cleaned. Was clean, cleansed."

DM: And you, you are sort of s- pulled up into the sky, and then you feel yourself disjointed, falling as rain, flowing down onto this landscape, washing away this acid, life springing up behind you as you flow from the mountains down to the rivers into the sea. Um, all of this, all of the ash, all of the blood, all of the fire, all of the, this corrosion being washed away.
DM: Water pooling now at the center o- at this pit that was the mesa.

DM: But somebody had to protect the land that was left. And you can f- you can see now, you can feel like the mesa starting to contract a little bit like a heart beating really. The... It's still a pool of water, it's not a mesa yet, but this whole sinkhole, canyon, cavern has now been filled in with this water that, that was you. And it's now starting to slowly con- beat, slowly contract like a heart.
Kenzo: And you know the, um, the place where, uh, um, [clears throat] we could access the other dimension, like the, um, sh- the Shakun's realm?
Kenzo: Is that... Where was that in this whole arc?
DM: Uh, that was in, that was in the mesa in the current day. You haven't seen anything that might represent that yet.

DM: So this water continues, um, to do this th- to do this thing. Slowly it begins to dry out, contract a little. So every time it, like, pulses like this, the pool gets a little bit smaller, and a little bit smaller, and a little bit smaller. And you can see the mesa start to stretch up, like the land almost starting to invert itself. What was a, what was a sinkhole now beginning to rise up from the ground. Everything's all, um, you know, everything's pretty barren at this point. The land's just been washed clean. And as the, as this, um, process begins, continues, um, the voice says again, "The land was and will be connected by the people who believe in it."

DM: Out of this... You can sort of... It's almost like you're watching this now in the reflection of this pool as the mesa is growing up around the pool. And now you start to realize that the water that's left behind is forming itself into this pool of water that you saw before. That's the portal to Shakun's, um, realm. So this is, this seems to be forming as it is. And reflected in that you see walking, turning a corner on a narrow track high in the mountains, seeing small trails of smoke rising in the distance from the fires of a small village. And you can feel the anticipation of hearing again the sounds of hammers against stone, the soft patter of young feet running over stone, the background murmur of the life of the small village.

DM: As you walk up this path approaching the village, you then see in this pool of water falling through the mountains, through the stone, emerging on an open plain, riding fast on a horse, um, your, a, a companion, a, a, a, a young boy riding beside you. Both of you, you and this boy running, racing across the plains, laughing at how fast you are going, looking around at home. Arriving in camp. Sitting down as the sun sets, talking to your family, acknowledging the land that supports you, that protects you, that provides for you. And then watching as the sun sets into the night sky full of stars, clear and bright, and a sense of calm then washes over you as for a moment you feel the sense of profound peace, and everything slows.

DM: And you come back now to this pool of water, and you can see the lines of energy that are starting to run out from the, um, running out from this, this, this pool and that start to gather and start to pull themselves together to form a fibrous mass in the center of the mesa. And it's somehow your energy, your, um, connection, your, the, the sort of echoes of the land, of your home, of, of peace and your emotions that settle on you that are also somehow pulled into this fibrous mass that's growing and forming into stone.

DM: Um, and somehow also the childhood of- The woman who was at the center of the mesa, who now you see Shakun forming around the stone. When she takes it, she then reaches into the, her translucent body and pulls out the heart and lays down. And as she lays down, you can see the mesa forming around her.

DM: And she places the heart down, growing bigger and bigger in size. And you can then see the, the web, the sort of fibrous mass of power of, of these webs that has coalesced into the Shakun's heart that you've seen before. And as it's placed, it springs up with this light that's illuminating the, the cavern that you're in, this sort of warm, reddish glow of sunset, and it races across all of Dunmar. And the narrator voice says again, "We will protect this land together." And you can feel the energy now flowing back and forth between you, between the heart, between everybody else who is, who you sense now outside and around, between Candrosa-

DM: ... between the acolytes who are helping with this ritual, um, between the Mystai elsewhere in Karawa, even those who are traveling. Although you can't quite tell where they are, but you can feel the kind of ebb and flow of energy with each beat of this heart now in its place in the, um, uh, in the temple here.

DM: And as your eyes snap open, standing in the fire, the blue fire of this water, not wet, seeing now the ref- the reflection in this pool, the images that you've seen b- that you saw once before, the, the images of, of the village track in the mountains, of running across the stars, and then, uh, running across the plains of stars. And then many, many, many others.

DM: Camps, um, tending horses, praying, a particularly delicious food, snuggling with your parents. Just images, and images, and images of what you realize must be the memories or the, the moments of peace and happiness of all the other Mystai that you are now connected to reflected in this pool as you stand up. And then Candrosa nods to you and says, "Welcome, my friends."

Kenzo: And do we feel, like, the, um, [clears throat] this kind of feeling of connections? It's sort of like, uh, um, the web is drawing from our strength? Or are we, like, how... Do we feel more connected to something and are, like, feel like an energy going through us? Is it dynamic, like give and take?
DM: Yeah, it's going through you. It's like y- you've, you're like a conductor. You're like a, a conductive... You're like a wire that's, that's transmitting this power from-

Kenzo: Uh, and can we... Is it, like, uh, is it like a communication network, too? Can you, like, sense other people in the network? Can I, like, you know, can you transmit messages or information through it?
DM: If you're, if you're close to them, you can identify, you can sense somebody is also connected.
DM: So you can identify other initiates-
DM: ... if you're close to them.
Kenzo: And I'm guessing we can also detect, like, disturbances to the force. You know what I mean? So it's like if there's some-
DM: Yeah, so if you, like-
Kenzo: ... a disruption or something like that, we can sense that.
DM: ... if the, like, p- you know, the energy flowing through you slows, or changes, or gets disrupted, or this, this protection gets broken somehow, yeah, you could definitely sense that.
Drikod: Mm. Drikod is just silent with all those connections and the visceral way in which he realizes how his village is and his home is connected to this larger world.
Kenzo: Tim, for Kenzo, um, is there any interplay between, like, Shakun, Bhishma, Laka? Like, is there, like, similar energy webs? Are they-

DM: Uh, so there's not similar energy webs. They're, they're quite, they're all quite different in the, in the way that they, the, the, the sort of mystical power of the divinities are manifest in the world.

DM: But one thing that I actually should have mentioned that you do notice is the vi- the vision of the, of the young girl racing across the plain and then coming into camp. You recognize the people that she came into camp with. They were Laka and Bhishma, were at camp waiting for her.
Unknown: And that was Shakun riding the horse.
DM: So that was Shakun riding the horse, yeah. That was her memory of childhood.

Kenzo: Hmm. Yeah, Kenzo, Kenzo kind of, you know, sits in meditative prayer, um, you know, attuning himself to this larger web of energy, um, reflecting on what he's seen, the history that was revealed going back, you know, to the... Did the, did the elven forest have a name?
DM: Uh, I have a, it did. I have an, I might have it written down somewhere. I don't know what it's called.

Kenzo: Doesn't matter. Doesn't matter. Is it, is it, um, is it the case that, like, the el- is the Elven Forest like a well-known thing? Does it, like, regular Dunmar people know that there used to be a forest here, or is that like not-
DM: It's not, I mean, it's not... Like obviously all the initiates of, of Shakun do.
DM: But it's not something that would be common knowledge.

DM: Most people would know that there was like, you know, an em- there was an old empire that used to be here. Most people would know Drankor. But the elves predate even Drankor, and most, most people have no i- most people would have no idea.
Drikod: Did Drikod sense any other Stoneborn as part of the initiated?
DM: Who are initiated? Uh, no. You are probably the first non-human-
DM: ... who has been initiated into... Well, at least who's currently alive. There might be... There th- uh, you wouldn't, you wouldn't necessarily be able to sense, um...

DM: Oh, actually, that's not true, 'cause in the, in the, like, um, in the, in the mirror at the end when you're s- yes, you would have seen a couple of other, um, memories of a childhood that reminded you of yours. Um, not people-

DM: ... you can sense, like currently in this web, but in that sort of last image where you were just seeing basically the recorded history of the whole sort of conne- set of connections that make up this, this web, you would have...
DM: Drikod would have caught, caught glimpses of a, of a handful, not more than... Certainly not more than a dozen and, and probably fewer than that-
DM: ... of childhoods in the mountains or, or, you know, high up. Definitely, um, the sorts of images that are very non-Dunmari and would be much more Stoneborn-like.
Drikod: Did I sense in any way, um, Entamba, the, the, the mountain spirit or the mountain-
Drikod: ... as, as we unders- as the Stoneborn understand it?

DM: No. The f- the f- the gods of the firstborn or, or of the elder races are quite distinct from the human gods. Um, so you didn't really sense... Like, this is a v- this was a very, um, human-centric ceremony. You didn't really sense... But, but you... I mean, you know, you've had experiences of Entamba that are kind of similar in the sense of the, of the sort of centered on the land kind of experience.
Kenzo: Is this, um, is the, uh, kind of feeling of the network, is it like constant? So sort of like, is it sort of like a background you can tune into it whenever you want?
DM: Like, it, it's not, it's not, uh, something you would be constantly aware of, but it's anytime you want, you can basically just, just-
DM: ... tune your consciousness to it, and you can feel that-
DM: ... like tingle of electric current running through you, basically.
Kenzo: And sorry, the, the moment when, like, it was born,
Kenzo: can you just describe that part one more time really quickly? Like, 'cause, you know, there was the fire happened, and then there was the, the, um, the water started filling in.
Kenzo: was that the key? Was that... Like, when, when was Shakun actually, like...?
DM: So, so the, the water sweeping everything clean is, is... was like Jeevali's tears. It's the, it's the sort of moment of, of the Dunmari settlement of the land.
DM: And then the sort of key moment is shortly after that when Shakun basically is... She's born human, but of a divine parent.
DM: And then during her lifetime is essentially, you know, deified, becomes a god. And it's that moment when she becomes a god that's like the swirling together of the-
DM: ... kinds of energy that makes, that forms the heart.
Kenzo: And you're s- 'cause in, in the first description you said there was a little boy riding a horse.
Unknown: Is this supposed to be the girl?
DM: Uh, the boy is her brother, Kotana, who was the first, uh, first ruler of the-
Kenzo: Ah. Oh, we're riding from the perspective of her.
Unknown: Like I see. I see. Okay.
Unknown: Got it. Got it. Got it. Okay.
DM: So he was like the first ruler of Dunmar.
DM: So it was like the division of the... He's the, he's the, the, you know, the mortal government, and she's the protect the immortal, protect against magic, defend the land kind of thing.

before: DM: [clears throat] Okay.
Unknown: [clears throat]

DM: So just jump right in. Um, so both of you have spent most of the... Both Drikod and Kenzo have spent most of the, the week, 10 days that you've, that you've all been just kind of hanging out in Karawa, studying and, and praying and, you know, every day, um, learning a little bit more about the, the history of Shakun and the sort of, um, mythos of her and her power, and also practicing and strengthening your connection to this web of power that, um, that maintains this, this defense of Dunmar. So it's a lot of, been a lot of like meditation and, um, just spending time sort of focusing on how power flows through this network of people.
after: Kenzo: Is Dunmar like a, like a hereditary kingdom?
Unknown: Like, are all the descendants...
Unknown: They're not.

DM: So it's, it's explicitly not hereditary. Historically, it's always been the gods ch- you know, it's like, I think we... Did we talk about this at one point? It's like the... It's like, um, or maybe it was I was talking to someone else. Basically, the gods choose the next ruler.
Unknown: Interesting.

interactions.title: Rai explains the broken jade and the dream’s meaning
lines: Kenzo: Okay. So sorry I didn't text back. That was like fucking awesome, though. That whole stretch was, like, really amazing. Um, so I think we left off when I directly asked Rai, like, "How do I return this stone to you?"
Kenzo: And then he was like, "This hasn't happened yet."
Kenzo: Like, we're in a place right now where there is no time, and it's sort of like future past events. It's all kind of merged together.
Kenzo: And, um, what w- and what was, what was the last thing?

DM: And then he, as he was speaking, he... You, you could see this. So there's been this, like, pale green light that's spreading out from his hand that is, like, in... So remember the two giants fighting?
DM: And the pale green light is, like, encapsulating and, like, protecting and shielding everybody from the thing he was fighting.
Kenzo: The, the human, the, the humanoid.
DM: And then as, as you speak and you see the ja- as you see his hand shatter into five pieces, the shield also fades.
Kenzo: Got it. Got it. Okay. Okay. All right. Hmm. And what happens af- after... What caused the shattering? Is it obvious, like, what happens to it?
DM: You holding up the jade and saying... You caused, you caused p- I mean, you didn't cause it to happen-
Kenzo: I caused it to shatter by holding it
DM: ... in real life, but in the dream world, you holding it up caused it to shatter because you-
DM: ... pulled it, you pulled that part of the world forward in time.
Kenzo: Got it, got it, got it. Okay. Okay. And, and what happened, what was Rai's reaction when the shattering happened? Like...
DM: Uh, initially fascinated, and then as... So he was, he looks, he watches in fascination as his hand shatters and says, "This has not happened yet. You bring a vision of a future yet to occur."
DM: And then as the shield begins to crumble, his expression turns from fascination to... Rai is not somebody who would be afraid of anything, but I would say maybe angry or, like-
DM: ... concerned. Um, like a sort of, "No good's gonna come of this" look.
Kenzo: Got it. Got it. So a- as that's happening and I'm noticing him do that, I h- I hold up the piece and I ask him, "How do I reunite the shield?"
DM: I do not know how. He doesn't know how. He doesn't know how this happened because he's not in the future, so he doesn't, he can't explain to you how to-

DM: Um, he says, "I wish I could tell you, but, but I am not where you are yet. Time flows in unpredictable ways here. The me you see and that," pointing at the piece of, of jade that you're holding, "come from different parts of the stream of time. You must find, you must find what did this in your time to understand how to undo it."
Kenzo: What pow- what, what force could possibly break this shield?
DM: Very little from this plane. But other planes, even I have not fully explored them.
Kenzo: Planes of the gods? Planes of other consciousness?

DM: Planes of the gods, planes of the fears and terrors of the early humans, devils, the abyss, the realms of dragons and giants. There is much out there me and my companions have tried to catalog over the years.
Kenzo: Yes, I've heard of him.
DM: There is much to study.
DM: I'm not sure right now.
Kenzo: Where's, where can I find Dimitaur?
DM: Hmm. Well, he is with me at the moment. But again, we speak across I do not even know how many years.
Kenzo: When, when is it where you are now?
DM: It is, it is the past, and you are the future. There are no counting of years in this place.
Kenzo: Do you c- do you commune regularly in the dream world? Can I find you here again?
DM: Perhaps. I think you brought me here. I think that brought me here, pointing at the jade.

Kenzo: Whatever is unfolding now in my time, here in the future to y- for your time, we- What have we unleashed? You battle a, a mighty warrior, a humanoid warrior. What, what has been unleashed now that this shield has been broken?
DM: The worst instincts of the Drankorian Empire's emperors.
DM: Not just that. A, a concern, a, a belief in the superiority of humans and of the pure Drankorian essence. I am afraid that may infect the world now.
Kenzo: Drankor has long disappeared in this time. The empire is in ruins in the jungle.
DM: But humans have not. There are always empires.
DM: And there is always the risk that they are corrupted at their heart.
Kenzo: Chardon is afoot. Today, my sense of what Drankor once was is embodied in the humans of Chardon. That's where I'm from. They seek items, they seek power.

DM: Drankor was, for many years, so much more than that. It was a beacon of hope. It was a beacon of a place where humans could be safe and protected from the evils of the world, where demons could be turned away at the gates. Chardon was once that, too. Chardon was a beacon of hope in my time.

DM: Nothing that happens here... Everything that happens here is a, an echo, a reflection. What you saw, nothing is literal. You may have seen yourself fighting for the, for a better Chardon. You may have seen my ancestors fighting for a better Drankor. These fights are never won. Never won permanently.
Kenzo: If I can find the other pieces and bring them together, will that change anything?
DM: It might. It might be, it might be something... It might be that you have to do this yourself. I cannot see all futures, cannot even see all the pasts.

Kenzo: If this is true, that in the future you are broken, your, your arm or your, you are broken in pieces, what signal, what sign can I use to try to find these other pieces? Do you know what, what binds you, your essence? How can I search?
DM: These are difficult questions. There is not... There is no spell, no wand you can wave that will magically answer how to find items of power.
Kenzo: What power does this have alone? I've only experienced wearing it, strange images. Um, I, I tell him the images, the, the tower. Where is this place?
DM: Hmm. I do not know what power that may have by itself. I... It is perhaps a part of me.

DM: And as you're speaking now, you can see behind him, like starting to claw out of the ground, this hand, giant hand, like of a 10 or 15 or 20-foot-tall person, but completely skeletal, that's just pushing down. And it's starting to rise up behind him, like this enormous skeletal giant growing out of the ground. And he says, "Look within yourself. If you have this, perhaps you have the means to find others or make others."

DM: We are connected somehow. And then the skeleton stands up and stands looming over him, and he sa- and he turns around and he says, "You must run now." And he starts growing again, and reaches up to, like, cast, cast some magic at the skeleton.
Kenzo: Do I recognize the skeleton?

DM: No, you don't recognize it. It seems, it just seems to be some other representation of, of this sort of tension at the heart of Drankor between, you know, the human superiority, greed, lust for power, and the, like, beacon of hope, protect everybody, safety from evil.

before: Unknown: Let's do it. Let's do it
DM: ... to run through the thing?
Unknown: Yeah.
DM: Okay. John, can you go back to the other room, and then we'll be back in a few minutes?
Drikod: Can do.
after: Kenzo: Is, is H-K-A-R, Hkar, is that, like, known?
DM: Yeah.
Kenzo: Is that like-
DM: That's where humans were created.
Kenzo: Okay. So is that, like, Dunmar, we... It's like common knowledge?

Drikod: Where's the list of those?
Delwath: In the party... Do you have the party treasure doc? Here, I can put it in the chat if people don't have the link. I have it open.
DM: I, I know that Schwartz wants... That Wellby wants the... So the ones that are highlighted haven't been claimed.
